title: Nothing forces us to say grace removes the power to act otherwise; it can be efficacious without that
source_text: XXXVIII. Praeterea vero quid cogit ut dicamus Deum, dum nos movet ad bona opera, a nobis auferre per gratiam suam potestatem aliter agendi, cum sine hoc constare possit gratiae divinae sua efficacia: nec desint sapientiae divinae rationes quibus praestet ut hoc agamus, idque certo ac infallibiliter, quanquam a nobis non tollat potentiam ad actum oppositum, & ad nostri etiam actus suspensionem?
pass_a_gloss: XXXVIII. But besides what compels us to say that God, while he moves us to good works, takes away from us by his grace the power of acting otherwise, since without this divine grace can have its efficacy: nor are reasons of divine wisdom lacking by which it may bring it about that we do this, and that certainly and infallibly, although it does not take from us the power to the opposite act, and to the suspension also of our act?
pass_b_english: Besides, what forces us to say that when God moves us to good works he takes from us, by his grace, the power to act otherwise? Divine grace can have its efficacy without this.
Nor does divine wisdom lack ways to ensure that we do the good, and do it certainly and infallibly, even though it does not take from us the power to the opposite act, or even to suspend our act.
